punchline: Feeling guilty about being angry gives you two emotions where there was one, which is why the book starts by asking you to stop grading them.
thirty_sec: Bradberry and Greaves open self-awareness with a plain rule: don't call an emotion good or bad. Judging it adds a second feeling, like guilt on top of anger. Then they ask you to use your body. In a calm moment, recall an event that stirred you and notice what your muscles, breathing and heartbeat did, so you can spot the same signal next time.
